kept.q: Which of the following best describes limiting friction?
options: It is the force that keeps an object permanently at rest
It is the maximum value of static friction just before an object begins to slide
It is the friction that exists only between two lubricated surfaces
It is the force that acts only after an object is already in motion
kept.explanation: Limiting friction is the greatest value that static friction can reach before the object starts to move. Once this value is exceeded, the object slides and kinetic friction takes over.
kept.pidgin: Limiting friction na the highest level wey static friction fit reach before the object go start to move. Once e pass that level, the object go begin slide and na kinetic friction go dey act.

kept.q: A technician uses a crowbar as a lever to lift a block of stone weighing 450 N from the ground. The fulcrum is positioned such that the load arm is 0.3 m and the effort arm is 1.2 m. Assuming the lever works as a perfect (frictionless) machine, calculate the minimum effort needed to just lift the stone.
kept.explanation: For a lever, effort x effort arm = load x load arm. So effort = (450 x 0.3)/1.2 = 112.5 N. This is the minimum force needed since the machine is assumed frictionless.
kept.pidgin: For lever, effort times effort arm go equal load times load arm. So effort be (450 x 0.3)/1.2 = 112.5 N. Na the smallest force wey go fit lift the stone since no friction dey.

kept.q: A wooden block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal laboratory bench. A horizontal pulling force of 20 N is just enough to make the block start sliding. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the coefficient of static friction between the block and the bench surface.
kept.explanation: At the point of just moving, the applied force equals the limiting frictional force, F = mu x m x g. So mu = F/(mg) = 20/(5 x 10) = 0.4.
kept.pidgin: Just as the block dey about to move, the force wey dem apply go equal the limiting friction, F = mu x m x g. So mu = 20/(5 x 10) = 0.4.

kept.q: A block-and-tackle pulley system at a construction site in Minna has a velocity ratio of 6. A worker, Musa, applies an effort of 100 N to raise a load of 480 N. Calculate the percentage efficiency of the pulley system.
kept.explanation: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 480/100 = 4.8. Efficiency = (MA/VR) x 100 = (4.8/6) x 100 = 80%. This shows the system loses some energy to friction since efficiency is below 100%.
kept.pidgin: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 480/100 = 4.8. Efficiency = (MA/VR) x 100 = (4.8/6) x 100 = 80%. Since e no reach 100%, e mean say some energy dey waste as friction.
